description: A large-scale dataset of 22,022 CT volumes with complete annotations for 167 anatomical structures, representing a significant advancement in both scale and coverage for whole-body CT segmentation.
license: Users of the CADS-dataset must comply with the individual licenses and terms of use for each source dataset
name: CADS-dataset
rai:annotatorDemographics: Three in-house medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist (JCP)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Automated outlier detection of pseudo-labels in shape space using neural implicit functions, and multi-strategy label generation through an ensemble selection mechanism.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Automated annotation methodology grounded in pseudo-labeling. Employs self-training through iterative model refinement, shape-guided quality control of segmentations, and fusion of the best-performing annotations from multiple segmentation approaches.
rai:dataBiases: Addresses systematic bias errors through targeted anatomical refinements, such as the costovertebral joint retrieval process that improves systematic omissions in existing datasets.
rai:dataCollection: Aggregates 22,022 CT volumes from 40 diverse sources, including public archives (e.g., TCIA and medical challenges), along with hospital cohorts. Includes 484 newly acquired head CTs and 586 newly released triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Addresses missing the part of costovertebral joints where ribs meet vertebrae by developing a specialized refinement process for the CADS-dataset rib labels to ensure anatomical correctness.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: CT scans that cover key anatomical regions throughout the body, including the brain, head-and-neck, thorax, abdomen, pelvis, and femur. Approximately 79% of the initial collection does not include any manual annotations.
rai:dataImputationProtocol: For the SAROS dataset which provides sparse slice-based 2D annotations, interpolation between the annotated slices is performed to create dense 3D per-slice annotations.
rai:dataLimitations: By directly excluding segmentations identified as low-quality from the training process, the dataset potentially eliminates cases involving pathological conditions that present atypical anatomical variations.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reorient all images to the standard RAS convention, resample to a uniform 1.5 mm isotropic resolution, simplify affine transformation matrices by removing rotation and translation components, and apply a Gaussian filter to facial regions.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Reorient all images to the standard RAS convention, resample to a uniform 1.5 mm isotropic resolution, simplify affine transformation matrices by removing rotation and translation components, and apply a Gaussian filter to facial regions.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Streamlines treatment planning through rapid organ delineation, enables automated organ volume quantification and detection of subtle anatomical changes in diagnostic radiology, and facilitates large-scale studies across diverse populations.
rai:dataUseCases: Anatomical landmark detection, cross-modality registration, anatomy-guided synthesis, longitudinal organ tracking, personalized anatomical modeling, radiation treatment planning, and large-scale population studies.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: nnU-Net framework, vesselFM, neural implicit functions
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Patient facial regions in newly acquired hospital head CT scans are obscured using a Gaussian filter (σ= 5 voxels at 1.5 mm spacing) to protect identity.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: Not applicable; annotations are primarily generated via automated pseudo-labeling and ensemble methods rather than independent human annotations per item.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No specific annotation platform mentioned for the dataset creation (automated pipeline used).
